source_locator: R428: pp. 141, 142; R061: section French & German campaign (1944-1945)
current_activity: Battle of Marseille: the German garrison surrenders to de Monsabert
notes: Event date: 28 August 1944 (CMH Riviera to the Rhine, p. 142; Wikipedia). Event definition: De Monsabert, commanding the division, rings Marseille; the 7th Algerian Tirailleurs plunge into the city on 23 August, and the German garrison surrenders formally at 1300 on 28 August. Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH) and Wikipedia). CMH Riviera to the Rhine ch. 8 p. 141: "his instructions to Col. Abel Felix Andre Chappuis, who commanded the 7th Algerian Tirailleurs, were flexible"; p. 142: "On the evening of 27 August, Schaeffer parlayed with de Monsabert to arrange terms, and a formal surrender became effective at 1300, 28 August"; Wikipedia, 3rd Algerian Infantry Division, section French & German campaign (1944-1945): "On August 15, 1944, the 3e DIA disembarked in Provence, at Cogolin in the Var, liberated Toulon and Marseille". Location: Marseille, Bouches-du-Rhône (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location support: the CMH history names Marseille for the division commander and its 7th Algerian Tirailleurs; Wikipedia names Marseille for the division; two source families. Commander: Maj. Gen. de Goislard de Monsabert commands the division until he takes over the II Corps on 2 September 1944 (CMH Riviera to the Rhine, p. 198, note 9; Wikipedia).

source_locator: R544: p. 322; R061: section French & German campaign (1944-1945)
current_activity: First French crossing of the Rhine, at Speyer
notes: Event date: 31 March 1945 (CMH The Last Offensive, p. 322; Wikipedia). Event definition: At the head of the First French Army, the division crosses the Rhine at Speyer before dawn on 31 March, starting with a single rubber assault boat. Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH) and Wikipedia). CMH The Last Offensive ch. 15 p. 322: "By 0230 on 31 March, infantrymen of the 3d Algerian Division at Speyer had found only a single rubber assault boat"; Wikipedia, 3rd Algerian Infantry Division, section French & German campaign (1944-1945): "On March 31, 1945, at the head of the 1st Army, the division crossed the Rhine in the region of Spire". Location: Speyer, Rheinland-Pfalz (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: both sources name Speyer (Spire) and the date. Commander: General Augustin Guillaume commands the division from September 1944 (Wikipedia).
